name: Bodak Skulk
tactics: The bodak skulk approaches foes undetected using spectral form and then waits for an opportunity to gain combat advantage. When it’s poised to attack, the bodak reverts to normal form and attempts to weaken a foe with its slam attack. It fixes its death gaze on the first enemy it weakens.

alignment.name: Evil
alignment.description:
Evil creatures don’t necessarily go out of their way to hurt people, but they’re perfectly willing to take advantage of the weakness of others to acquire what they want.
	Evil creatures use rules and order to maximize personal gain. They don’t care whether laws hurt other people. They support institutional structures that give them power, even if that power comes at the expense of others’ freedom. Slavery and rigid caste structures are not only acceptable but desirable to evil creatures, as long as they are in a position to benefit from them.

weaknesses.name: Radiant
weaknesses.details: ; a bodak skulk that takes radiant damage cannot weaken a target until the end of its next turn

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Agonizing Gaze
traits.details: a creature in the aura that makes a melee or a ranged attack against the bodak skulk takes 5 necrotic damage before the attack roll is made and takes a -2 penalty to the attack roll.

auras.name: Agonizing Gaze
auras.details: a creature in the aura that makes a melee or a ranged attack against the bodak skulk takes 5 necrotic damage before the attack roll is made and takes a -2 penalty to the attack roll.

hit.description: damage plus 2d6 necrotic damage, and the target is weakened until the end of the bodak skulk’s next turn
if the target is weakened, it is reduced to 0 hit points; otherwise, the target takes 1d6 + 6 necrotic damage and loses 1 healing surge

effect.description: The bodak skulk turns invisible and gains the insubstantial and phasing qualities . It can do nothing but move in spectral form, and it can return to its normal form as a free action.
